releases.title: Visual database manager and project bundles
releases.summary: Code Studio adds context-based Explorer actions, portable Adminerva project bundles, and a phpMyAdmin-inspired visual data workflow while retaining the existing SQL learning engine.

changes.text: File and folder creation, rename/move, delete and open actions now live in a right-click context menu instead of occupying permanent Explorer toolbar space. Shift+F10/Context Menu keyboard access is supported.
ZIP exports now include adminerva-project.json with project configuration, database data and design artifacts. Importing an Adminerva bundle restores those alongside the source files.
Adminerva DB now has a visual Browse view with tabular rows plus Insert, Edit and Delete actions for tables with primary keys.
The Structure view shows column order, names, data types and primary-key metadata for the selected table.
The SQL console is now one database-manager view rather than the entire database experience, and remains connected to CRUD evidence/history.
Selected tables can be exported as CSV, and + Table opens a CREATE TABLE starter in the SQL view.
A compiled Adminerva POS Management System bundle demonstrates multi-file Java Swing, layered OOP design, product/cart/sales workflows, and companion Adminerva DB tables with seed data.

releases.title: Code Studio command bar refinement
releases.summary: Removes another layer of vertical chrome by consolidating project commands into the project header and simplifying Studio navigation.

changes.text: Language, Java run mode, Save, Format, project actions, autosave state, XML Lab, Minerva and Run now live in the same project-header row beside Project settings instead of a separate Code toolbar.
Application and Terminal were removed from the primary Studio tabs because the Desktop/Web preview and Terminal remain directly available inside Code output.
Persistent drag/drop and keyboard-shortcut instructions were replaced by a compact Explorer information tooltip so the file tree gets more vertical room.
The consolidated command bar stays single-row on wide screens and becomes horizontally scrollable on narrower layouts rather than introducing another persistent toolbar row.

releases.title: Code Studio workspace density
releases.summary: Reclaims vertical and horizontal workspace space across Code Studio, fixes the unused dark strip beneath the editor, and reduces navigation/footer overhead.

changes.text: Code Studio now restores the missing flex layout on the active studio shell so Code, Swing preview, Design and Database workspaces fill the available height instead of leaving an unused dark strip above the footer.
Project identity, project tabs and project settings controls use a denser layout with smaller vertical padding while retaining the same actions.
Language/runtime controls, Save, Format, project menu, XML Lab, Minerva and Run controls are more compact and the redundant Code heading is removed from the toolbar.
Explorer controls, file tabs, path bar, terminal header, input area and desktop runtime status use a denser IDE-style layout to return more space to code and application output.
Design, Database, Evidence and Monitor surfaces now use wider content areas, smaller headers and tighter cards so primary workspaces are less cramped.
The shared Adminerva footer is compacted only on Code Studio pages, including smaller padding and hidden footer credits, preserving the standard footer elsewhere.
The shared Code Playground breadcrumb/navigation strip is reduced in height specifically for the IDE page.

releases.title: Code Studio guest access and workflow polish
releases.summary: Guest users can now build named local projects in Code Studio with transparent limits, while signed-in and guest project workflows receive safer reset, import/export, autosave and storage-status behavior.

changes.text: Guests now use the same named-project Code Studio experience with Code, Design, Database, Application, Terminal, Evidence and Monitor surfaces instead of the legacy single-draft editor.

Guest projects are local-only and limited to three projects, twenty-five files per project, about 300 KB per project, five Adminerva DB tables and one hundred rows per table. Limits and shared-browser storage behavior are shown in the interface.
Project cards and the active project header now show storage mode, file count and approximate project size. Guest projects never attempt cloud synchronization.
Reset restores the selected project template, including its starter files, database schema and design artifacts, instead of replacing it with a generic language file.
Exports use the project name, imports obey the active project tier limits, and imported files are saved into the named project with a recoverable local undo copy.
Design artifacts autosave with the project while retaining the explicit preview and save controls.
Guest export and snapshot-adjacent controls no longer depend on the authenticated-site global loading helper, and authenticated-only page scripts remain excluded from public guest routes.

releases.title: Adminerva Code Studio
releases.summary: A project-first programming workspace for building Java console apps, Swing desktop applications and information-system prototypes with integrated design, SQL practice, evidence and run monitoring.

changes.text: Code Playground now opens to named projects with recent-project cards, project settings, local autosave and private cloud project synchronization.
Create Java Console, Java Desktop, Java Information System, Blank Java, Python Console or Web projects from a guided configuration wizard.
The Java Information System template starts a multi-file Swing project with model, service and UI structure plus project design and data workspaces.

Project-scoped SQL learning database supports table creation and CREATE, INSERT, SELECT, UPDATE, DELETE and DROP practice with persistent project history. JDBC source evidence remains tracked separately rather than being simulated as a real JDBC driver.
Use Case, Class, Sequence and Architecture diagrams live beside the code project and render from Mermaid diagram source.
Project evidence summarizes observable Java concepts, SQL CRUD activity and design artifacts while clearly distinguishing learning evidence from official competency assessment.
Run history records reported execution time and memory for console runs, with transparent handling when browser desktop JVM telemetry is unavailable.
Console and Swing desktop execution remain part of the same Java project. Desktop runtime stays labeled Beta/technical evaluation while the project model and UI are productionized.
Existing local playground drafts remain importable, practice sandboxes and shared snapshots retain the legacy direct-editor workflow, and guest playground behavior is preserved.

releases.title: Simpler assessment evidence and class review
releases.summary: Direct student evidence revisions, easier class approvals and attribution review, stronger grading and evaluation workflows, and restored lesson printing.

changes.text: Reopen and approve eligible evidence for a selected section and assessment in batches, with refreshed submission status and per-student exceptions.
Revise selected commits after an instructor reopens evidence without withdrawing. Confirm a newer verified project checkpoint when necessary.
Students can explain shared-device or mismatched GitHub commits in a visible form. Teachers inspect claims; authorized administrators record audited attribution decisions.
Compact assignment cards and guided commit selection, with filters, counts, expandable previews and secondary withdrawal controls.
Clean evaluations remain unpublished grades ready for the existing publication process. Review-only suggestions are retained only when teacher attention is needed.
Adaptive handling of large contribution histories and diffs, improved renamed-file scope, and more precise evidence limitations.
Export an individual contribution assessment package for external evaluation and import validated responses into appropriate unfilled review fields.
Copy section-specific reminders for students missing independently verifiable individual contribution evidence.
Restore stable legacy browser printing, continuation formatting and timetable compatibility without modifying existing saved lessons.
Show release notes and updates appropriate to each account role while preserving privacy and existing notification preferences.

releases.title: Reliable class review and refreshed Adminerva
releases.summary: More reliable class review, evidence gathering and grading, clearer mobile layouts, consent-based usage analytics, refreshed owl branding, and stronger release checks.

changes.text: Single Assessment is the primary Gradebook workflow, combining legacy submission receipts with section-scoped evidence, grades and publication status.
Gather missing evidence within the assessment window without overwriting saved student work. Project checkpoints remain distinct from verified individual contributions.

Re-evaluate eligible unpublished system drafts while preserving earlier results, stop after the current learner, and inspect complete exception lists. Teacher edits and published grades remain protected.

Corrected repository matching and stale source paths, improved original-commit and merge-context evaluation, and made large-diff limits explicit. Shared project code alone does not establish individual credit.
Restored Gradebook bulk actions and Review & Grade, fixed a class-grid loading race, simplified RepoFetch setup, and open the review editor when it is ready.

Historical report discussions render reliably, comment controls follow ownership, and Administration Overview makes support triage easier to find. Administrator release announcements prevent duplicate delivery for the same version.

Anonymous product-usage analytics requires consent and can be controlled in Account settings. Names, emails, learner identifiers, repository links, commit references, grades, feedback and URL query values are excluded; advertising signals are disabled.
Staff settings and administration views wait for verified access, and connection settings hide stored credentials. Section-based authorization remains in place.
Gradebook uses clearer mobile cards, feedback opens in a centered dialog, and shared layouts have more consistent spacing and navigation. Homepage motion respects reduced-motion preferences.
The supplied transparent owl and circular emblem now appear across navigation, public pages, sign-in, study-owl controls, notifications, browser icons and installed-app icons.

Valid discovery, approval, reopening, withdrawal and resubmission work with up to twenty selected commits while preserving access restrictions and immutable history. Quality checks now run before updates are merged.

releases.title: Classroom workflows and student follow-through
releases.summary: Teachers get clearer class review, school administration and student follow-through tools, with safer settings and better project and slide organization.

changes.text: Gradebook brings each learner's submission, evidence, grade and publication status into one class review view. Bulk approval checks checkpoint ancestry, and evaluation saves private suggestions for teacher confirmation rather than writing grades.

A School Administration overview connects student records, teacher assignments, school configuration and operations. Reports can be marked as internal, copied as support-ready Markdown, exported, and closed while preserving their history.
Teacher work is separated into Repository Management and Lesson Planning. Account menus, help links, privacy controls, interface preferences and Website updates push settings are easier to find.
Teachers can assign Practice Packs, named projects and Improvement Plans. Students see assigned work in their existing workspaces, with selected-student projects scoped to their assignees.
Code Playground supports precise file and folder ordering and named, pinned, duplicated, restored and cleaned-up cloud versions. Slide Navigator supports drag reordering and structural Undo/Redo.
Student profile ownership requires a verified email claim, versioned activity grades keep their audit history, and grading alerts cannot be reassigned across students or sections.

releases.title: Integrated review workflow and complete playground organization
releases.summary: Teacher review is consolidated into one grading flow with clearer publication states and subject-focused workspaces, while Code Playground completes project ordering and cloud version management.

changes.text: Evidence review, contribution context, selected changes, system evaluation draft, teacher scoring, feedback and publication now stay in one primary workflow instead of competing standalone review tools.
Each learner now shows the next useful action, such as review submission, grade approved evidence, continue a private grade draft or view a published result.
Saved teacher grades are identified as Graded draft until explicitly published. Published results have a separate status so private work is not mistaken for student-visible feedback.

Teacher access can optionally include subject focus in addition to assigned sections. Repository Management, assessment lists, submissions and gradebook views hide unrelated subjects while existing teachers without a subject focus keep their current view.
Assessments retain and display their subject, and subject-focused teachers create and edit assessments within their assigned subject choices.
Older Evidence Review, Contribution Inspector and Group Inspector links now open the integrated Review & grade workspace while preserving available learner and assessment context.
Files and folders support precise manual ordering with before-or-after insertion feedback, plus existing folder and project-root moves. Explorer order persists through saved and restored work.
Cloud versions can be named, pinned, unpinned, duplicated, restored, renamed and deleted. Confirmed cleanup keeps the newest 10 unpinned versions together with every pinned version.

releases.title: Clearer workspaces and stronger playground organization
releases.summary: Staff Home, Repository Management and Lesson Planning are separated more cleanly, Submission Inbox can identify graded work, and Code Playground adds drag-and-drop project organization plus basic cloud version management.

changes.text: Staff Home, Repository Management and Lesson Planning are distinct destinations. The former Educator Hub is renamed Repository Management and its navigation focuses on assessments, submissions, grading, repositories and analytics.
The shared website header is more compact to recover vertical workspace space while retaining the same primary controls.
Submission Inbox can show and filter a derived Graded state when a matching grade record exists, without replacing the underlying evidence lifecycle states such as Submitted, Approved or Reopened.
Students can drag files and folders into folders or back to the project root. Valid drop targets are highlighted while dragging.
Students can rename or explicitly delete their own cloud versions. Saved source contents remain immutable; only the version label metadata can be changed.

releases.title: Simpler educator workflows and notification accuracy
releases.summary: Teacher workflows are consolidated around a smaller Educator Hub, combined class and Practice analytics, a clearer Review & Grade flow, compact modals, and corrected notification wiring.

changes.text: A student receives a returned-for-changes push only when the evidence record has a fresh audited reopen revision with a reviewer, timestamp and matching reason. A status transition alone is no longer enough to send the alert.
Gradebook filters obsolete review warnings such as 'No grade has been recorded' once a score exists, and removes stale pre-approval draft warnings after the grade has been freshly reviewed.
Published records label retained cautions as Review notes so valid provenance warnings remain visible without implying that the current grade is missing or unpublished.
The score-details view is treated as a centered modal instead of inheriting the right-side drawer layout. Desktop and mobile bounds keep it centered and within the viewport.

Teacher alerts now recognize both ordinary resubmissions and the important reopened-to-submitted transition, so a corrected student evidence package does not disappear from the teacher notification flow.
Publishing and unpublishing a grade now use grade notifications. Unpublishing reports that the released grade was withdrawn for revision instead of being confused with an evidence return.
Report status changes and replies notify the original reporter, including private bug reports, while staff audiences still receive the appropriate report notifications.
Commit-reclaim alerts can open Assessment Evidence Review directly, and backend push destinations use the same allowlisted Adminerva pages as the in-app notification router.

Student submission updates and recipient-scoped report replies are no longer hidden by the notification visibility filter. Returned-for-changes alerts come only from audited backend records rather than client-side evidence-state inference.

Device push preferences separate submissions, grading alerts and report replies instead of routing unrelated events through the submission switch. Existing accounts default the new categories on until changed.
Assignment notifications now cover both deployment and target-section changes and can notify again when a section is legitimately re-added later.

Teachers rely on their per-user notification feed instead of broad section-restricted Firestore collection listeners that could fail authorization. Administrators retain broad fallback feeds for historical records.

Teacher navigation is task-based: Teaching, Review, Resources and School setup. Standalone evidence inspectors and legacy graders are removed from primary menus while their underlying engines remain available inside the integrated workflow.
Class Analytics and Practice Analytics are combined into one Analytics workspace with Class results and Practice & learning views. The old Practice Analytics URL redirects to the combined page.
Academic analytics now queries only assessments and grades visible to the teacher's assigned sections instead of attempting broad collection reads that can fail section-scoped permissions.
Current and earlier Practice analytics load only the teacher's assigned class roster instead of listing the full student collection.

The primary review workspace is reduced to Inbox, Evidence, Review & Grade and Observed activity. Repository and contribution engines remain inside evidence/review details or the collapsed legacy area instead of competing as separate tools.
The saved-plan dialog is more compact: one close control, refresh in the header, a small older-lesson recovery strip and more vertical space for the lesson list.

Signed-in users return directly to their saved teacher or student workspace instead of loading the sign-in page first. Centralized Auth Guard now performs any necessary role correction once, using replace-style navigation, and is enabled on Assessment Studio and Review & Grade.

releases.title: Reliable push alerts and cleaner mobile notifications
releases.summary: Real assessment and teaching alerts use the same proven background delivery path as the test ping, notification cards are more compact and identifiable, Practice prompts are clearer, and shared mobile layouts are more resilient.

changes.text: Real assessment, returned-submission, grade, teaching-submission, grading and report alerts use the service-worker data-message path already proven by the test ping, including foreground handling and persistent real notifications.

Teachers and administrators can enable device push from Account Settings. One Teaching alerts preference covers student submissions/evidence, grading attention and report/reply events without adding a new preference schema.
Teacher evidence submission and resubmission alerts include the student's name and assessment title instead of generic wording, and those events can now fan out to enabled devices.
Notification cards use a denser layout with compact type and time metadata, a small unread marker, shorter Save controls, and Settings moved into the header to reduce wasted vertical space.
Shared compact-screen rules improve notification-panel sizing, flex and grid shrinking, form/media containment, safe-area spacing and horizontal overflow behavior without changing desktop layouts.
Write-the-output missions now explicitly ask for only the exact output or requested value; the explanation is shown after a correct answer instead of being requested inside an exact-match field.

releases.title: Safer evidence, notifications and release reliability
releases.summary: Evidence review, resubmission and push alerts are more reliable, student access is tighter, saved work is safer across accounts, and new status messages stay compact instead of crowding the page.

changes.text: Teachers can verify all submitted evidence commits with one checkbox. Individual commit verification remains in a collapsed exception area for shared, disputed or excluded commits.
Teacher commit diffs no longer load automatically. Selected commits stay compact until Preview changes is opened, reducing long scrolling and missed verification controls.
When evidence is reopened, the affected student sees a targeted notification using the authoritative evidence record, including the teacher's reopening reason and a link back to My Assignments.

Student evidence commits and the project checkpoint are separate. The checkpoint may be a later teammate commit as long as it contains all selected student evidence; the checkpoint itself does not become individual credit.

Adminerva verifies Git ancestry before accepting a student evidence submission and identifies selected commits missing from the chosen checkpoint, preventing checkpoint mismatches from first appearing during teacher approval.

The latest repository revision is suggested as the project checkpoint for new submissions. Students can choose another revision when needed, while selecting only their own relevant commits as evidence.

Teachers can return a submitted evidence package for correction when approval cannot proceed. The required reason is retained in audit history, shown to the student, and the student must resubmit before approval.

The Return for student changes button now works for submitted evidence instead of silently ignoring the click. Submitted, approved and instructor-proposed evidence all use the same audited return/reopen handler.

Teachers can filter the Submission Inbox by class section, submission status and assessment in addition to search. Supported evidence states include submitted, approved, reopened, needs review and withdrawn.
Each Submission Inbox card now shows a clear status badge so teachers can scan approval and resubmission state without opening the student review page.

Students can opt in a browser or mobile device to receive push alerts for newly assigned assessments, submissions returned for changes, and published or corrected grades. These three push categories are enabled by default at the account level; the browser still requires one explicit permission action per device.

Student notification settings separate in-app inbox visibility from device push delivery. Students can turn individual push categories off, disable push for the account, or disable only the current device without affecting other registered devices.

Adminerva includes a web app manifest and Firebase messaging service worker so supported mobile browsers can receive background notifications. iPhone and iPad push remains dependent on the web app being added to the Home Screen and the user granting notification permission.

The existing authoritative notification pipeline now supports optional push fan-out. Push is best-effort and does not replace Adminerva's in-app notification history. Device registrations are account-scoped and removed from the current browser when the user signs out.

Student Settings includes a Send test ping action for the signed-in account's registered devices. Test pings bypass Adminerva notification history, use a short-lived test tag, and attempt to close after about 15 seconds so device delivery can be checked without leaving permanent inbox entries.

Device push opt-out now persists, sign-out removes the current account registration without silently becoming a permanent opt-out, account switches cannot reuse another user's registration, and reconnect attempts are bounded.

Student assessment reads are prepared for section-scoped authorization, private repository evidence can use the student's linked GitHub access, and suspended roster entries preserve history without retaining student workspace admission.

Lesson edits gain a local recovery draft, schedule fallbacks and presentation defaults stay with the signed-in teacher, and personal coding-assistance keys stay separated by Adminerva account on shared browsers.

Lesson recovery state now appears as a compact header badge, notification settings use shorter device states, and duplicate roster-import guidance is hidden from the visual layout while remaining available to assistive technology.

releases.title: More reliable Review & Grade and student evidence
releases.summary: Review student work with fuller repository evidence, clearer proposed scores and teacher checks, safer submission access, and a simpler evidence-reopening workflow.

changes.text: Firebase sign-in restoration no longer looks like an account switch while Review & Grade is loading, preventing valid teaching results from being discarded during normal page startup.

Grading alerts, student submissions and teacher-visible reports are read through assigned-section access instead of broad staff queries that Firestore rejects. Teacher grading alerts no longer depend on a new composite index.

Evaluation responses distinguish malformed output, response-limit truncation and other provider stop reasons. A malformed or truncated first response is retried once in a shorter format. Criteria can now award evidence-supported points while reserving only genuinely unresolved points for teacher confirmation.

The evaluation timeout now starts after repository evidence is retrieved instead of during GitHub loading. The service has enough time for a normal response and one compact retry, with a visible still-processing status for slower evaluations.
Review & Grade uses shorter system-focused status messages, a clearer Retry evaluation action and explicit confirmation that failed evaluation attempts do not replace the teacher's score or feedback.

The evaluation request includes a rubric-shaped response schema, and the server source is prepared to forward that schema when the school evaluation function is deployed. Browser-side validation still checks evidence references and score bounds before suggestions can be used.
RepoFetch, the teaching access adapter and notification modules use refreshed asset versions so browsers receive the repaired files instead of stale cached modules.
RepoFetch explicitly uses the Adminerva logo as its page icon instead of causing a missing favicon request. The Tailwind CDN production warning remains a separate styling-build task.

Review & Grade evaluates the student's verified primary XML screen together with supporting Activity, Manifest, Gradle, drawable, theme and resource changes from the same approved commits. Shared project source remains context and cannot independently earn individual credit.

Before rubric evaluation, Adminerva runs bounded XML and Android resource checks for constraints, component IDs, placeholders, touch dimensions, resource resolution, Activity/layout linkage, Manifest registration, dependencies and invalid Android resource naming. Best-practice findings do not automatically become rubric deductions.

A single unresolved visual or runtime check no longer removes an entire rubric criterion from the draft. The system shows a proposed score from supported evidence, the points still awaiting teacher confirmation and the possible score range. Teachers can adjust the final score after evidence review or classroom observation.

Referenced bounded PNG, JPEG and WebP repository assets can be included in evaluation when the deployed school evaluation service advertises image support. This can verify visible labels or artwork without adding another grading panel; exact native Android rendering remains a separate check.

For Android XML UI assessments, verified substantive student XML screen commits can serve as the student's individual screen responsibility when no more specific responsibility note exists. Missing teammate screens remain shared project context rather than an automatic individual deduction.

Teacher review now uses one clear Reopen for student changes action for approved evidence and instructor-discovered proposals. The reason field becomes visibly required during reopening, and the page explains when reopening is needed so students can replace commits and checkpoints before resubmitting.

releases.title: Reference folders restored to the teacher workspace
releases.summary: Use earlier reference folders in your teacher library and retain their selections when opening saved lessons.

changes.text: The original teacher's earlier reference folders and saved reference text are restored to that teacher's library with the same folder IDs. Existing lesson reference links remain compatible.

The library waits for verified staff sign-in, identifies the current account, uses account-scoped caching and provides visible loading failures with a refresh action. Each teacher retains their own library.
Saved lesson reference-folder selections are retained while the folder list loads, and both older inline references and newer folder documents remain readable.

releases.title: Original school lesson-plan formatting restored
releases.summary: Print and export lessons using the familiar merged school table, original blue headings and a compact school banner.

changes.text: Restores the legacy merged table cells, Arial Narrow typography, original blue heading color and column proportions. Removes the added session strips, fragmented text rows and repeated column headings.

Exports the school banner with explicit proportional dimensions and applies the original table styling directly to exported cells, keeping the signature table borderless and retaining useful export results and downloads.
Updates with a recorded publication timestamp display their actual date and time. Earlier date-only releases show the date without an invented midnight time.

releases.title: Legacy lessons in the original teacher account
releases.summary: Recover older saved lessons directly in the teacher workspace, with clearer account ownership and all school years visible.

changes.text: The verified original teacher can recover earlier school lessons when opening Saved Plans without visiting the administrator account. Recovery always targets that teacher's UID, preserves existing saves and avoids duplicate legacy copies.

All school years are shown by default. The signed-in account, recovery results, recovered labels and archived counts make lesson ownership and availability clearer, with a retry action when recovery cannot finish.

releases.title: Clearer lesson printing and Google Docs export
releases.summary: Print complete lesson plans with continuous landscape tables and keep a usable export even when Google needs attention.

changes.text: Landscape printing uses bounded table rows and repeated column headers instead of session-wide rowspans, reducing mostly empty continuation pages while preserving lesson content and signatures.

Google Drive authorization is reused during the current page session. Upload failures show Google's response and HTTP status. A created document remains accessible when final formatting needs review, with Word and HTML downloads available as alternatives.

releases.title: Connected classes, playful practice and one teaching workspace
releases.summary: Choose a class once, review and grade in one workspace, explore real project files, and earn Practice Points through varied missions.

changes.text: Class, assessment, Group/Individual and target selectors drive one inline inbox, source browser, contribution view, evidence review, teacher grade and manual activity tool. Switching panels retains the selected context.

School catalogs and assigned roster sections now populate planning, scheduling and admissions. Administrator entry to Teachers restores missing original-teacher assignments and safely recovers metadata-attributed lessons. Unattributed records have an explicit recovery flow that preserves originals.
Sessions persist across navigation. Existing accounts continue to their workspace, public guides provide return links, and temporary access failures offer retry without signing out.

Lesson, slide and assessment generation share a server-managed school connection. The administrator saved connection can be reused without exposing the school key to teachers, with individual request allowances and bounded concurrent requests.

Routine evidence and grading audit notes are prepared from the selected review. Additional notes are optional; exceptional revisions retain reasons. Assessment Studio starts with a usable rubric and optional student instructions.

A shared mission map offers choice, exact-answer, ordering, matching and debugging activities. Missions award 20, 30 or 40 Practice Points with difficulty-based mistake deductions and a half-reward completion minimum. Replays do not duplicate rewards; earlier progress remains in history.

Visitors can preview missions and use the shared code editor. Verified signed-in guests can save ranked practice. Public alias rankings are optional; class progress and teacher season reports remain scoped to the class.

A real file and folder explorer supports moving, renaming, ZIP import/export and portable project paths. The toolbar groups secondary actions. Compiler runs show stages, support cancellation and stop waiting after 45 seconds while preserving drafts.

Device size, orientation, zoom, component tree, property editing, templates and local resource values support layout experiments. Common sibling constraints, guidelines, cards and scroll containers have improved browser previews; unsupported Android behavior is identified.
Public demo entry, role-home search and continuation, an optional owl interaction and long-page shortcuts make navigation easier. Notification and motion preferences live in account settings.

releases.title: A clearer workspace from sign-in to school setup
releases.summary: Find Home and Workspaces directly, follow clearer school setup, and recover interrupted practice with useful next steps.

changes.text: Prediction and completion controls remain hidden until a server challenge is ready. A session conflict now leaves a clear message instead of a visible button that cannot act.
Home, workspace switching and the current page are visible across the website. Menus work with keyboard and touch, and shared forms, status messages and mobile layouts use consistent styles.
Catalogs have search, filters and clearer forms. Teachers use section checkboxes with roster counts. Existing teacher assignments are preserved when an access request is approved.
The Teachers link opens teacher management. CSV import supports keyboard selection, drag and drop, file replacement and a clear record limit.
Student and staff homes highlight the next task. Sign-in explains which email to use, prevents repeated sign-in windows and gives clearer recovery messages.

Connection preferences now save with clear verification feedback. Application connection details reflect the deployed configuration. Reference PDF processing stops after errors or a bounded wait and supports retry.
Connection fields belong to the signed-in account. Switching accounts or signing out clears the previous browser values, and staff pages restore only that account's own saved connection preferences.
Pending assignments include unfinished revision work. Account loading errors offer retry, and learner practice reviews restore the selected student's notes without stale results.
The ZIP library loads before the code editor's module loader so project archive export and multi-file packaging can access the correct constructor.
The page now describes server-saved completions and tab-only reflection drafts accurately. Practice XP remains separate from school grades.

releases.title: Checked practice, clearer review and assigned teaching access
releases.summary: Practise across 300 guided missions, follow class-only alias rankings, move scored sessions safely and use a clearer individual review workflow.

changes.text: Four courses each contain five modules with fifteen missions. Checked completions earn automatic unique-mission XP without teacher approval or optional activity sharing. Replays remain playable without duplicate XP; earlier self-recorded progress stays separate.

Moving an active scored session requires your confirmation and recent sign-in. Saved points remain intact, older sessions cannot submit new credit, and shared devices do not cause automatic cheating penalties.

Administrators assign teaching sections explicitly. Teacher review and analytics use assigned class records and credential-free roster copies. Unprepared older shared records remain restricted for administrator review.

Approval and reopened selections refresh in place. The step bar aligns with the modal heading. Evaluation drafts distinguish supported subtotals from unscored criteria and explain the next teacher check. Shared group completeness does not establish individual credit.

Verified new accounts can request student or teacher access while using limited local guest tools. Administrators make audited role decisions and manage sections, subjects and pathways. Requests do not grant access automatically.

Saved lessons restore their document settings within each teacher workspace. Reviewed repository overviews use pinned source samples and explicit saves; they do not establish individual authorship or automatically change grades.

Use the question-mark menu for page help, support, the Wiki and public updates. Release versions are separate from their dates. School grades, optional activity sharing and practice XP remain distinct.

releases.title: Personal teaching workspaces, clearer review and simpler navigation
releases.summary: Separate teaching files by account, use a clearer review workspace, search student evidence and manage optional activity preferences from Account Settings.

changes.text: Lessons, timetables, slides and planning defaults stay separate for each signed-in teacher. A newer save from another tab is not silently replaced. Older shared records remain preserved for administrator review.
Administrators can authorize verified teacher emails, assign analytics sections and disable access without deleting saved teaching files. This does not send invitation emails or create passwords.

Administrators select an instructor in Teacher Analytics. Published results are distinct from private drafts, and missing scores are not treated as zero. Operational reports and diagnostic trails remain in Administration Analytics.
The brand and account controls adjust on smaller screens, notifications stay inside the viewport, and a consistent footer links tutorials, the Wiki, public updates and privacy.
Review steps stay easy to reach while scrolling, and save and publication actions wrap on small screens. Saving privately and publishing remain separate teacher decisions.
Temporary evaluation outages and incomplete responses keep teacher edits intact, explain retry timing and offer manual grading. Account and source limitations still require instructor verification.

Compact score previews open detailed feedback without crowding tables. Publication shows the number of reviewed drafts, checks each saved record again and reports interrupted work without automatically resuming.
Navigation and notifications stay above the slide toolbar. Opening a different menu closes the previous panel, and Escape returns to the menu button.
Filter students by section and search names or GitHub usernames. Current selections stay visible while searching; loading another review remains a deliberate action.

The question-mark menu brings together public updates, reporting, support and the Wiki. Optional activity choices appear on home visits, with an account-based reminder opt-out and controls in student and staff Account Settings. Hiding the reminder never enables sharing.

Clearer learning and operations views distinguish missing data from zero results, offer refresh controls and keep class results separate from unavailable activity sources. Repository history is labeled as a limited sample, not proof of individual contribution.

releases.title: Google Docs export connection update
releases.summary: Lesson Planner export uses the current website connection, requests narrower file access and explains interrupted authorization.

changes.text: Google Docs export uses the current website authorization client instead of an older connection. Project services and user authorization are still required.
Exports request access only to files used with Adminerva, not all of your documents. Declined or missing permissions stop the export before a document is created.
Blocked or closed authorization windows show clearer guidance, and the loading indicator finishes when export preparation or upload ends.

releases.title: Reliable evidence editing and a preloaded review workspace
releases.summary: Reopened commit selections update live, review panels load together, and older approvals can receive explicit individual verification.

changes.text: Instructor reopening updates the open student selection without requiring a page reload. Editable commit checkboxes and checkpoints remain available; approved evidence remains protected.
Equivalent saved evidence no longer causes a false changed-evidence warning because fields arrived in a different order. Real concurrent changes still block approval and keep unsaved review notes.

Evidence, pinned source, group status, history and contribution details preload in parallel using shared bounded reads. Opening accordions reveals results instead of starting nested page applications.

Instructors can explicitly revise contribution verification on older approvals without changing student-selected commits. Changes create an audit revision, invalidate older drafts and require unpublishing protected grades first.

Evaluation explains missing approval or verification requirements and becomes available after an instructor records verified individual work. Scores and feedback remain private drafts until deliberate teacher publication.

releases.title: Review, learning tools, Help and optional analytics
releases.summary: A clearer grading workspace, XML layout practice, lesson-linked slides, public guides and privacy-conscious learning activity.

changes.text: Review committed evidence and pinned source, use an optional Adminerva Auto Checker draft, and save teacher scores and feedback in one workspace. Copy suggestions deliberately and publish grades separately.
Older selected commits remain editable after withdrawal. Approved evidence needs instructor reopening, and review navigation no longer covers evidence buttons.

XML Layout Lab previews a supported Android XML subset in the browser. Practice has personal points, independent teacher review and optional alias-only class snapshots; these do not change assessment grades.
Saved lessons open editable slide starters with source-version details. Existing slide edits are not silently replaced.
Open contextual tutorials, the public Adminerva Wiki and curated patch history throughout the website. Published releases appear in the account notification inbox.
Teacher learning summaries and administration monitoring are separate. Activity sharing is optional and excludes typed content and credentials. Activity observations never become grades.

Administrators can configure optional background cleanup and learning-summary refresh with recorded policy changes. The service needs separate server activation; saving settings does not deploy it. Consent changes are checked again before summaries are saved.
Loading status stays visible while overlapping key processes finish. Clearer page names preserve existing links, and repeated preferences saves no longer inflate visit counts.

releases.title: Help, learning activity and clearer analytics
releases.summary: Public tutorials, optional activity sharing, separate learning and system monitoring, and clearer loading feedback.

changes.text: Open a page tutorial or browse the public Adminerva Wiki. Wiki and patch-history links are available throughout the website, including public pages.
Teacher Analytics focuses on learning; Administration Analytics focuses on system monitoring and support. Administrators select configured instructors in the teacher view.

Choose whether to share module visits and approximate active time. Optional diagnostic actions attach to administrator reports only when explicitly selected. Activity observations never become assessment grades.
Account checks and key learning, review and analytics processes keep a visible status while overlapping work finishes.
Teacher Analytics, Group Inspector and the older Activity Grader use clearer page names. Existing links continue to open the matching workspace.

releases.title: Clearer review and student learning tools
releases.summary: Three clear teacher review sections, editable evidence selections, XML layout previews, practice points, and lesson-linked slide starters.

changes.text: Read public patch history and receive a notification for each published release in your account inbox.

Review evidence, use an optional Adminerva Auto Checker draft, and enter the final teacher score in three sections. Suggestions copy only when accepted. Protected grades can be unpublished for revision in the same workspace.
Previously selected older commits remain available for editing. Editable selections can be cleared before resubmission, and instructions and rubrics expand when needed.
Edit Android layout XML and preview supported widgets, dimensions, colors and parent-edge constraints in a sandboxed browser view. The simulator is a learning approximation, not Android Studio.
See personal practice points. Instructors can review missions and publish opt-in, alias-only class standings; practice points do not change assessment grades.

Open a saved lesson in the Slide Editor and build editable starter slides without an external service. Saved decks retain their source lesson version; newer lesson versions do not silently replace slide edits.

releases.title: Review & Grade workspace
releases.summary: A simpler teacher review workspace, individual contribution checks, and protected student evidence revisions.

changes.text: Review selected evidence, checkpoint approval, evaluation drafts and group details from Review & Grade.
Evaluation drafts distinguish verified individual contributions from shared project completeness. Teacher review is required; grades are never published automatically.
Students can revise or withdraw evidence before approval. Approved evidence requires instructor reopening, with previous submissions retained.
Account controls fit narrow mobile screens more reliably.
